command: Edit this picture. It is a cut-paper character on cream paper; the flat magenta areas are where their left arm (its sleeve and round hand) was cut away to make a cut-out puppet. The toddler is seen from the side, running towards the viewer's left and leaning forward, and their other arm does not show: their left arm was stretched out level behind them, from their shoulder under the ear to the round hand at the right edge, over the plain paper. Repaint ONLY the magenta areas, as what lies underneath the arm: their back, from behind their neck down to the tunic, closed by the same thick dark brown-black outline as the rest of them, painted in exactly the same style, colours and soft shading as their body beside the arm (the cream linen tunic, and the soft lavender shade of its far side below the arm). Their back runs down from their neck in one smooth curve to the tunic's back edge: out to their shoulder and tunic, not in at the sleeve's edge. Shade with colour, as the sheet does: the side away from the light in the soft lavender, never grey or black. Paint the linen tunic of their body with the same fine paper grain the sheet shows on them beside the arms: a fine, even speckle through every flat area of colour, never smooth flat colour. There is no arm now: no sleeve, no hand, nothing magenta left. Where the magenta lay outside their body, it becomes the plain cream paper. Keep every other pixel exactly as it is: the same head, tuft of hair, ear, face, tunic, legs, sandals, ground shadow, size, position and framing.
